gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build route file is still present, but current master is missing readable `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig` and `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader_contract.zig`, so this build surface is an adjacent stale scaffold rather than an honest replayable gate for the atomic64 packet.
The dedicated runtime survey gate keeps the direct sample packet and the current missing shared-loader readback fail-closed instead of implying live runtime parity.
The bounded sample keeps the direct atomic64 starter and guarded lifecycle parity evidence reviewable under the `lib/atomic64_test.c` anchor.
The sample descriptor and `runSelftest()` contract keep the roadmap selftest hook surface explicit without implying a live runtime substrate.
The dedicated module tests keep the bounded starter lifecycle and direct sample-backed module gate reviewable on current master.
The narrow diff gate keeps add, sub, bitwise, swap, compare-swap, and add-unless expectations from `lib/atomic64_test.c` machine-checkable without widening the runtime packet.

A bounded loader scaffold still keeps the atomic64 entry symbol, exit symbol, and handoff-plan shape reviewable, but current master no longer exposes readable `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig` or `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader_contract.zig`, so the scaffold cannot currently support an honest shared-loader replay claim.

The roadmap's full runtime module lifecycle parity cannot be claimed while current master is missing readable shared runtime-loader files, so the atomic64 lane must stay in a direct-starter-only posture before any deeper runtime-substrate follow-through.
